answers.answer: It is a condition on occupying an approved child restraint system (under 14 CFR § 91.107 regarding safety belts, harnesses, and child restraint systems), furnished by the operator or a specified person, rather than a standalone general manufacturing requirement for all seats. It applies provided that, except as provided in paragraph (a)(3)(iii)(B)(4), seats manufactured to U.S. standards between January 1, 1981, and February 25, 1985, bear that specific label.
No, the source states passively that the approved child restraint system "must bear the label" without identifying the manufacturer as the party legally obligated to perform the labeling action.

No, the label requirement is only one condition under paragraph (a)(3)(iii) introduced with "provided that" and "Except as provided in paragraph (a)(3)(iii)(B)( 4 )", and does not establish authorization to use the restraint without meeting other applicable conditions.
